summary: Implemented Sha256ChecksumVerifier and full unit-test suite. All 34 tests pass (7 new). FileNotFoundException message includes the file path. Case-insensitive comparison confirmed via uppercase hash test.

comments.note: SHA256.HashDataAsync is available on .NET 8+ and used correctly here. The buffer size (81920) matches StreamReader defaults, which is idiomatic. No issues observed in touched files.

FileNotFoundException.Message and FileNotFoundException.FileName are separate properties. FluentAssertions WithMessage only matches the Message string, not FileName. The implementation includes the path in the message string to make it testable, which is slightly non-standard but pragmatic given the constraint.

metrics.test_coverage: 7 new tests covering: match, case-insensitive match, mismatch, empty-file match, empty-file mismatch, missing file, cancellation

comments.note: Null filePath is not guarded — File.Exists(null) returns false, causing FileNotFoundException instead of ArgumentNullException. Low risk: callers are expected to supply a valid path. No AC failure.

IChecksumVerifier interface doc states 'lower-case hex string' but implementation accepts case-insensitively (OrdinalIgnoreCase). The broader acceptance is beneficial. Minor doc/contract inconsistency, no AC failure.

Malformed expectedSha256 (e.g., non-hex characters or wrong length) is not validated — returns false rather than throwing. Correct per interface contract (false = no match), but could mask caller bugs silently.

summary: Reviewed 2 files (Sha256ChecksumVerifier.cs, Sha256ChecksumVerifierTests.cs). 0 Critical, 0 High, 0 Medium, 2 Low, 1 Info. All OWASP Top 10 categories checked. Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: [Low] A02 — Cryptographic Failures: string.Equals(OrdinalIgnoreCase) is not constant-time. File: Sha256ChecksumVerifier.cs, line 33. For file-integrity use (expected hash is public/known), this is not a practical timing-attack vector. Remediation: no immediate action needed; document that this method must not be repurposed for HMAC or secret-value comparison without switching to CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals().

[Low] A03/A04 — Injection / Insecure Design: filePath is passed to File.Exists() and FileStream without path canonicalization (e.g., Path.GetFullPath). File: Sha256ChecksumVerifier.cs, lines 21–28. In the provisioning context all paths are application-constructed, mitigating this in practice. Remediation: callers should canonicalize and validate paths before passing to VerifyAsync if ever sourced from untrusted input.

[Info] A04 — Insecure Design: null filePath is not guarded; File.Exists(null) returns false, causing FileNotFoundException instead of ArgumentNullException. File: Sha256ChecksumVerifier.cs, line 21. Remediation: add ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(filePath) as first statement (defence-in-depth).
CancellationToken: correctly forwarded to SHA256.HashDataAsync — not swallowed. Test VerifyAsync_CancellationRequested_ThrowsOperationCanceledException confirms propagation. No issues.
Temp-file fixture (TempDirectory): uses Guid.NewGuid().ToString('N') for unpredictable directory names and deletes on Dispose. No world-readable predictable path issues. No issues.

summary: Code review passed. Sha256ChecksumVerifier is minimal and correct: SHA256.HashDataAsync, FileShare.Read, await using, OrdinalIgnoreCase, diagnostic exception message. Tests cover 7 scenarios including cancellation and empty-file edge cases with clean TempDirectory fixtures. One Fix-Forward applied to IChecksumVerifier doc comment. No blocking issues.

comments.note: Fix-Forward applied: IChecksumVerifier.VerifyAsync param doc said 'lower-case hex string' but the implementation performs OrdinalIgnoreCase comparison. Updated the expectedSha256 param doc in IChecksumVerifier.cs to read 'hex string (64 characters); comparison is case-insensitive.' This is a documentation-only fix — no behavioral change.

Minor: the cancellation test writes a 4096-byte file and pre-cancels the token before calling VerifyAsync. At that size, SHA256.HashDataAsync may complete before the cancellation is observed on fast hardware, making the test potentially non-deterministic. Low risk — the test was passing and the API does check the token. Not blocking.
